precepts.text: Captain: he removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged. Just because you think you are wise in your older years, the Lord will take away your understanding, so no one should trust what an old fool says. Daniel's wisdom was called upon as a young man; Paul told Timothy to let no man despise his youth, a younger man who became an elder over the church. Many of the prophets were called young and set over congregations because the aged, who were supposed to have the wisdom, did not; they judged incorrectly, took bribes, and were engulfed in their lust like the elders in the history of Susanna. Our leaders here in Israel United in Christ have proven themselves through time and through the rigorous scriptures, and that is why we give them the honor they deserve.
precepts.point: But wisdom is the gray hair unto men, and an unspotted life is old age. There is a reason the Messiah called you in your old age so the younger men can teach you; some of you in your old age are no good, your mind is gone, and the Messiah sent the young men to help you. Instead of embracing it you say, you cannot teach me anything. Then you are going to die in your sin, brother.

note.label: Worldwide Upheaval: The Coming Crisis

precepts.why:
We are supposed to learn from the aged. But as Wisdom of Solomon 4 says, honourable age is “not that which standeth in length of time, nor that is measured by number of years”, and Job shows why: “He removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged.”

Look how the Lord deals. Just because you think you are wise in your older years, he will take away your understanding, so that no one should trust in what an old fool says. Our people think that because you are up in age you automatically get the respect. It is not about the age. It is about the wisdom the Lord placed in you, and the Lord can remove that from you.

That is why Daniel's wisdom was called upon while he was a young man, and why Paul instructed Timothy not to let anyone despise his youth: he was a younger man who became an elder over the church. Many of the prophets were called young and set over congregations to lead the people, because the aged, who were supposed to have the wisdom, did not. They were judging incorrectly, they were in briberies, and like the elders in the history of Susanna they were engulfed in their lust. So the Lord called younger men to do what the older men were not doing.

So “wisdom is the gray hair unto men, and an unspotted life is old age.” There is a reason the Messiah called you in your old age so the younger men can teach you. If instead of embracing it you say, I'm too old for these young men to tell me what to do, you cannot teach me nothing, you are going to die in your sin, brother. Our leaders in Israel United in Christ have proven themselves through time and through the rigorous scriptures, and have applied them, and that is why we give them the honor they deserve.

precepts.text: The deceived and the deceiver are his; the judgment is the Most High's, not ours.
precepts.point: Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
“With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.” Israel today cannot put the prophet or dreamer of dreams to death; we are in the land of our oppressors, and no kind of violence is advocated. The judgment belongs to the Most High, not to us: both the deceived and the deceiver are his, and he will deal with them.

What is ours is to mark them and avoid them, and to put those men and those women out from among the body. The one who has spoken to turn you away from the Lord your God is left in the hand of the one whose he is, with whom is strength and wisdom.

precepts.text: He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them.
precepts.point: He increaseth the nations and destroyeth them; the only reason they got big numbers is that they are being fattened for destruction.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
“He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them again.” He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them; the only reason they got big numbers is that they are being fattened for destruction.

All the men of Gibeon were mighty, and the kings gathered all their hosts, and Joshua took all these kings and their land at one time because the Lord fought for Israel. The nations are enlarged and then straitened again; that is his doing, and it is not unjust.

precepts.text: With him is strength and wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver are his. The Most High used these heathen women, and later Delilah, to get Samson caught up with the Philistines so that he would end up destroying them.
precepts.point: The Most High is in control of everything, good and evil alike. Even affliction that comes on his people is his tactic to make them seek him and repent; nothing anybody does can alter the outcome he has already ordained, for he declared the end from the beginning.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

precepts.why: “With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.” Samson was deceived by the heathen women he lusted after, and later by Delilah; yet the deceived and the deceiver both belong to the Most High. He used these heathen women to get Samson caught up with the Philistines so that he would end up destroying them. Samson’s flaw was the occasion the Lord sought against the Philistines, who at that time had dominion over Israel. That is the basis of the whole story: the Lord was behind all of it, pulling the strings.

precepts.text: With the Most High is strength and wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver are His.
precepts.point: The Most High used the deceiver to prove whether the man would keep the charge, and disobedience under that dispensation carried the penalty of death.

note.label: 1 Kings 13: The Man of God and the Two Prophets

precepts.why:
“With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.” The old prophet who lied and the man of God who was lied to were both in the hand of the Most High.

That is why the word of the Lord could come through the very prophet who had deceived him, as they sat at the table: “thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers.” The Most High used the deceiver to prove whether the man of God would keep the charge he had been given, “Eat no bread, and drink no water.”

He did not keep it, and under that dispensation disobedience carried the penalty of death. A lion met him by the way and slew him, and his carcase was cast in the road with the ass and the lion standing by it, neither eaten nor torn. Deceiver and deceived were both his, and the judgment was his.

precepts.text: With the Most High is strength and wisdom, and the deceived and the deceiver are his, for he leadeth counsellors away spoiled and maketh the judges fools.
precepts.point: The Most High put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets and spoke evil concerning Ahab. The deceiver as well as the deceived are under the hand of the Most High, who uses the lie to bring the judgment he has already declared.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

precepts.why:
“With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.” He leadeth counsellors away spoiled and maketh the judges fools.

Micaiah saw “the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.” The Lord asked, “Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead?” A spirit came forth and said, “I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.”

“Now therefore, behold, the Lord hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these thy prophets, and the Lord hath spoken evil concerning thee.” The deceiver as well as the deceived are under the hand of the Most High. He used the lie of the four hundred prophets to bring on Ahab the judgment he had already declared.

precepts.text: If the prophet be deceived when he hath spoken a thing, the Most High hath deceived that prophet and will stretch out his hand and destroy him from the midst of his people Israel.
precepts.point: A lot of people think the Most High is all hugs and kisses, roses and daisies, but he is loving and he will also lay it to you; the devil, Satan, works for the Most High, and nothing can be done without him allowing it, for they are his.

note.label: Job 12: With God Is Strength and Wisdom

precepts.why:
“And if the prophet be deceived when he hath spoken a thing, I the Lord have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand upon him, and will destroy him from the midst of my people Israel.” The Most High himself deceived that prophet, and then stretches out his hand and destroys him.

That is “the deceived and the deceiver are his.” This is a heavy precept, because the Most High uses anybody he wants, and the deceived and the deceiver are ordained by him. A lot of people think the Most High is all hugs and kisses, roses and daisies, but he is loving and he will also lay it to you. With him is strength and wisdom.

precepts.text: The Most High on his throne asks who shall entice Ahab, and a spirit comes forth and says he will go be a lying spirit in the mouth of all Ahab's prophets, and the Most High sends him to prevail.
precepts.point: A lot of people think the Most High is all hugs and kisses, roses and daisies, but he is loving and he will also lay it to you; the devil, Satan, works for the Most High, and nothing can be done without him allowing it, for they are his.

note.label: Job 12: With God Is Strength and Wisdom

precepts.why:
Micaiah saw “the Lord sitting upon his throne, and all the host of heaven standing on his right hand and on his left. And the Lord said, Who shall entice Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead?” A spirit came out, stood before the Lord, and said, “I will go out, and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And the Lord said, Thou shalt entice him, and thou shalt also prevail: go out, and do even so.”

The Most High on his throne sends the lying spirit and tells it to prevail. So the deceived and the deceiver are his: the devil, Satan, works for the Most High, and nothing can be done without him allowing it, for they are his. He uses anybody he wants. He breaketh down and it cannot be built again; he shutteth up a man and there can be no opening. He is loving, and he will also lay it to you.

precepts.text: Thou shalt grope at noonday as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways, describing how our people stagger though the light is brightest.
precepts.point: Look at what they did to the northern kingdom, taking away the heart of the chief, the mighty warriors, infiltrating them with alcohol and diseases, then sending them on their way with smallpox blankets so they stagger like drunken men; many of our northern kingdom brothers, especially Gad, deal with drunkenness, opium, and the war on drugs, but we keep the commandments and are coming back to be straightened out.

note.label: Job 12: With God Is Strength and Wisdom

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.” Our people stagger though the light is brightest. That is “They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man”; this is Deuteronomy 28.

He increaseth the nations and destroyeth them; he enlargeth the nations and straiteneth them again. This is us, Israel, for the curses destroyed us to the point where we do not realize we are the Israelites, God's chosen people, and then he heals us back up again. You see the aged of the people lose their wisdom and the strong lose their might, like Muhammad Ali and others we thought were noblemen for the nation of Israel.

Look at what they did to the northern kingdom: taking away the heart of the chief, the mighty warriors, infiltrating them with alcohol and diseases, then sending them on their way with smallpox blankets so they stagger like drunken men. Many of our northern kingdom brothers, especially Gad, deal with drunkenness, opium, and the war on drugs. Oppressed and spoiled, and no man shall save us; but we keep the commandments and are coming back to be straightened out.

precepts.text: The deceived and the deceiver are the Lord's, so do not try to deceive yourself.
precepts.point: This is so the house of Israel may go no more astray from Him nor be polluted any more with their transgressions, but be His people and He their God.

note.label: Ezekiel 14: Idols in the Heart and the Four Sore Judgments

precepts.why:
Job says of the Most High, “With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.” Both belong to Him. That is exactly what is said here: if the prophet is deceived when he has spoken a thing, “I the Lord have deceived that prophet”. The Lord Himself did it.

So do not try to deceive yourself in this truth. When we get counsel, we should take it and keep it moving. The Lord stretches out His hand upon that prophet and destroys him from the midst of His people Israel, and “the punishment of the prophet shall be even as the punishment of him that seeketh unto him”: both bear the punishment of their iniquity.

All of it is so that the house of Israel may go no more astray from Him, nor be polluted any more with their transgressions, but be His people and He their God.
